subject: Elara Health — Sudden latency/500 spike and request throttling
messages:
From: Samir Desai <sam@elarahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@elarahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate + latency spike affecting our production integrations

Hi Rachel,

We started seeing a serious degradation in our integration metrics since ~07:45 PDT. Between 07:45 and 08:05 our service saw:
- 15% 5xx rate (predominantly 503/429)
- p95 latency jumped from ~1.8s to ~6s
- sustained throughput dropped ~30% even though request volume stayed flat

Attached is a small sample of error responses and request IDs (elara_error_samples.csv). Our ops team is getting alerted and customers are seeing failed requests in critical flows (claim ingestion).

We did not change anything on our side. The timing coincides with a scheduled quota window change you pushed for other accounts yesterday (we were notified about tenant-level quota housekeeping). Could that have affected us?

We need immediate mitigation (temporary unthrottling or a quota bump) and a short blameless postmortem. Please loop in whoever owns rate/burst policies. This is impacting active customers.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Integrations
Elara Health

--
Attachments: elara_error_samples.csv (CSV sample of request_id, timestamp, status, model, tokens)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <sam@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + latency spike affecting our production integrations

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up and for the sample. I'm escalating immediately.

Quick ask while we triage: can you share a single request_id and the exact timestamp (to the second) for one failed request so we can trace it in our logs? Priya/your team already attached a good sample which helps.

Marissa and Karthik — looping you in. Karthik, please treat this as P1: confirm whether this is throttling (rate/burst) or a different platform issue and advise immediate mitigations. Marissa, I'll need an exec note ready for Elara leadership once we have the mitigation plan.

Proposed immediate actions (please confirm):
- Temporary +40% quota for elara-health account for 72h
- Disable strict burst safety valve for this tenant while we investigate
- Enable fallback to the 2nd model variant (lower-cost, lower-latency) for in-flight requests if needed

I have attached a skeleton mutual-action-plan (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) to capture commitments.

I'll update Samir right after we have confirmation on the short-term unblock.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + latency spike affecting our production integrations

Quick technical findings from initial triage (logs & config):
- Observed 429s/503s correlated with token_bucket exhaustion on the tenant token bucket.
- The tenant burst_window value for Elara is configured as 60s (recent change deployed 2026-10-15 00:12 UTC). Expected production baseline is 300s.
- With a 60s window and our refill logic, short bursts from their workload consume credits faster and trigger the safety valve repeatedly; when the bucket empties, requests are immediately rejected until the refill cadence recovers — this creates the p95 spike and apparent throughput collapse.

Immediate actions taken: 
1) Applied emergency +40% quota to account elara-health (effective now).
2) Temporarily set burst_window -> 300s for elara-health (rolled back the recent 60s change).
3) Enabled model fallback routing for in-flight requests to the cached model variant (lower latency, verified warm cache).

Evidence attached: throttle-config-diff.patch (diff of burst_window and quota changes). I also pulled sample request traces tied to the IDs in elara_error_samples.csv and uploaded them to the incident drive.

Next steps I recommend (with owners & ETA):
- Ops (Karthik) will monitor error rates & p95 for the next 3 hours and report 30-min cadence (ETA: 13:00 PDT).
- Product (config owners) to add a guardrail preventing burst_window regressions for tenant-scoped changes (Owner: infra-config, ETA: 10/20).
- Engineering to run a backfill test simulating Elara traffic profile across burst_window ranges to validate safe defaults (Owner: runtime team, ETA: 10/23).

I'll revert the emergency quota change to the agreed level after 72h unless Samir requests otherwise — I'll coordinate with Rachel for the customer-facing timeline.

--
Karthik
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <sam@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@elarahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 16:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + latency spike affecting our production integrations

Samir — quick update and next steps.

What we saw: short bursts in your traffic exhausted the tenant token bucket because a config change yesterday set burst_window to 60s (the default for the rollout) instead of the 300s baseline we use for production tenants. That caused repeated safety-valve tripping and the 5xx/429 pattern you observed.

What we did (already active):
- Emergency +40% quota for 72h (will revert unless we agree otherwise)
- Restored burst_window to 300s for your tenant
- Enabled model-fallback to a warm cached variant for in-flight requests

Operational plan & asks:
- Karthik will monitor and provide status every 30m for the next 3 hours.
- We'll produce a short postmortem with root cause and preventive actions by EOD Tue (10/20).
- Marissa will send an exec note to your leadership with the immediate mitigation summary and timelines (incoming shortly).

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as a high priority. Please confirm receipt; if anything continues to fail, forward one failed request_id and timestamp and we'll trace immediately.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
